title: Proactive SKU probing and kernel fallback policy for attention prefill/decode
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Reduce tail latency and cost variance for mixed-SKU fleets (H100/L40S/A10) under MIG-partitioned hosts by adding a lightweight runtime SKU probe and a deterministic kernel fallback policy for attention prefill and decode paths. Background: We observe sporadic 95/99th tail regressions when a request lands on a MIG slice with lower clock or when NVLink/Thermal behaviour reduces available bandwidth. Existing kernel selector prefers max-throughput kernels based on offline profiles; when runtime conditions differ this causes high latency and retry churn. Approach: 1) Add a sub-2ms probing step on slice acquisition that runs a micro-attention inference (short prefix/short decode) to fingerprint latency and KV-cache warmup characteristics for that slice. 2) Extend kernel selector to accept a runtime hint: observed_probe_profile=(high-throughput|balanced|latency-optimized) and pick from precomputed kernel candidates including quantized/packed-attn and tiled-attn variants. 3) Define explicit fallback policy: if observed tail latency or decode latency exceeds baseline by X% (tunable) during initial N requests, automatically switch to fallback kernel variant and emit a routed-metric. 4) Integrate clocks and MIG metadata: include GPU clock state and MIG slice size in the probe metadata to avoid repeated probing when migrating within same slice affinity. 5) Keep probe budget bounded (2ms per warm allocation, up to 10ms total per allocation window) to avoid impact to P99 SLA. Trade-offs: - Pros: faster adaptation to heterogenous run-time conditions, reduced tail, clearer telemetry for regression detection. - Cons: slightly higher allocation latency due to probes, increased selector complexity and testing burden, more kernel binaries to support. Metrics: target 20-40% reduction in 99th prefill latency in mixed-SKU clusters for sequences >512 tokens; keep mean latency delta <= 3%.
acceptance_criteria: Probe executes in <2.5ms median on H100/L40S/A10 for a 32-token micro-attn workload
Kernel selector can switch to fallback within 3 requests and emit a routed_metric event
End-to-end P99 prefill/decode latency improves >=20% in our mixed-SKU perf harness
Probe budget enforcement prevents more than 10ms added to any allocation path
New telemetry (probe_profile, selected_kernel, slice_clock, probe_latency) landed in central metrics and available in console
updates: 2026-02-28 - Maya Chen: Created ticket. Captured initial telemetry findings from customer clusters showing 95/99 spikes when requests are routed to A10 slices with MIG fragmentation. Proposed micro-probe approach and fallback definitions.

2026-03-02 - Rafael Gomez: Spike implemented prototype probe library. Initial microbench shows median 1.6ms on H100, 2.2ms on L40S, 3.8ms on A10 (A10 needs tighter budget). Decided to cap probe to 2.5ms and mark A10 may use single-sample probe only.

2026-03-04 - Priya Nair (SRE): Reviewed runtime impact. Concern: allocation path adds latency for cold starts. Suggested doing probe asynchronously when warm reuses detected and adding conservative default kernel for new customers.

2026-03-05 - Rafael Gomez: Implemented runtime hint plumbing in selector; added kernel candidates list to model shard manifest. Added opt-in flag runtime.probe.enabled default true on dedicated fleets; recommended false for strict low-latency tenants.

2026-03-07 - Carlos M. (Perf): A/B plan drafted: 20% traffic to probe-enabled selector across three clusters (H100-only, mixed H100/A10, L40S-priority) for 72h. Success criteria defined in acceptance_criteria.
2026-03-09 - Design review: Maya provided UX for console visualization of probe profiles and selected kernel per route. Action: Add per-route override to disable probing and to pin kernel variant.

2026-03-10 - PR opened: runtime#4215 implements probe scheduling and fallback policy with feature flag. Running CI and extended perf harness. Requesting review from @kyle and @ana for kernel correctness and stability tests.
